question: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX) in platelets, and because mature platelets cannot synthesise new COX protein, the antiplatelet effect lasts for the entire platelet lifespan of approximately 7–10 days.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Aspirin's irreversible COX inhibition in anucleate platelets means the antiplatelet effect lasts 7–10 days (the platelet lifespan). This is the pharmacological basis for stopping aspirin 5–7 days before major surgery and for its once-daily dosing in antiplatelet therapy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Aspirin acetylates and irreversibly inhibits both COX-1 and COX-2. Platelets are anucleate and cannot regenerate COX-1, so the antiplatelet effect persists until new platelets are produced from megakaryocytes — approximately 7–10 days. This is why aspirin is typically stopped 7 days before elective surgery to restore normal platelet function.
